title: Sarga Thirteen — verses 1–148
html:
Title of the sarga: none — the colophon of the edition gives no title for this sarga. Metre: - 1–63 — upajāti (a mixture of indravajrā ——⏑——⏑⏑—⏑—— and upendravajrā ⏑—⏑——⏑⏑—⏑——; 11 syllables per pada); 12–13 — anuṣṭubh (8 syllables per pada; a quotation from the Kurma Purana); 39 — mandākrāntā (————⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑——⏑——⏑——; 17 syllables); 42 — vasantatilakā (——⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑⏑—⏑——; 14 syllables); 46 — Ramananda's Bengali song (rāga bhairavī). - 64–114 — svāgatā (—⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑⏑——) intermixed with rathoddhatā (—⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑—⏑—); 11 syllables per pada. - 115–125, 128–134, 138–144 — viyoginī (odd padas ⏑⏑—⏑⏑—⏑—⏑—, 10 syllables; even padas ⏑⏑——⏑⏑—⏑—⏑—, 11 syllables); 119, 126–127, 135–137, 147 — upajāti. - 145, 148 — śārdūla-vikrīḍita (———⏑⏑—⏑—⏑⏑⏑——⏑——⏑—; 19 syllables); 146 — vasantatilakā.

Total verses: 148.

Contents of the passage: the southern pilgrimage; the conversation with Ramananda; the return to Puri; the gathering of the devotees.
- 1–8 — the way south; Shrirangam: the chaturmasya in the house of Trimalla Bhatta; autumn.
- 9–13 — a brahmana devoted to Rama grieves over the abduction of Sita; the Lord shows him the verses of the Kurma Purana about the shadow Sita.
- 14–16 — the meeting with Paramananda Puri; he goes to Puri, the Lord to the Setu.
- 17–19 — seven palmyra palms are embraced and go to heaven.
- 20–30 — heretics try to allure the servant Krishnadasa; the Lord wins him back.
- 31–33 — Rameshvara at the Setu; the Lord turns back.
- 34–49 — the conversation with Ramananda on the way back, on the Godavari. The verse on renunciation — "this is external"; the verse nānopacāra… — "external"; the song pahilahi rāga… on the highest oneness of the Two; the embrace; several days of conversation "on the path of realisation".
- 50–59 — Puri: the Snana-yatra; the anavasara; the Lord goes away to Alalanatha, and the devotees search for Him.
- 60–61 — again on the Godavari: four more months with Ramananda; at the onset of winter the Lord returns to Puri together with him.
- 62–71 — Kashi Mishra (he sees the Lord four-armed), Vishnudasa, Pradyumna Mishra.
- 72–77 — a grove reminiscent of Vrindavana: the creepers as dancers; the Lord's dance.
- 78–88 — Prataparudra in the grove: he glorifies the rasa dance; the embrace; "Who are you?" — "Your servant."
- 89–109 — Shikhi Mahiti, his brother Murari and his sister Madhava-devi (Madhavi-devi); Shikhi's dream; the meeting in the Jaganmohana; the embrace.
- 110–126 — the arrival of the Bengalis. The line of Madhavendra Puri and Ishvara Puri; Paramananda Puri in Navadvipa with Shachi and Acharyaratna; Kamalananda; the journey to Puri with Gadadhara and Jagadananda; the Lord bows to Paramananda; Vidyanidhi, Acharyaratna.
- 127–136 — Shivananda with Murari Gupta; Raghava; Govinda becomes [the Lord's] servant; Bhavananda ("you are like Pandu") and his five sons; Vaninatha.
- 137–144 — Purushottama Acharya becomes Svarupa Damodara.
- 145–148 — Vakreshvara, Vasudeva Datta, Bhagavan Acharya; the Lord's fame spreads; Satyaraja, Raghunandana, Narahari and Mukunda arrive.

Verse 1

एवं स तीर्थाटनकौतुकेन
दीनैकबन्धुः करुणैकसिन्धुः ।
ततो ययौ भाग्यवतीमवाचीं
स्वनामरत्नग्रहणोत्सवोत्कः ॥१॥

evaṁ sa tīrthāṭana-kautukena
dīnaika-bandhuḥ karuṇaika-sindhuḥ |
tato yayau bhāgyavatīm avācīṁ
sva-nāma-ratna-grahaṇotsavotkaḥ ||1||

evam — thus; saḥ — He; tīrtha — to the holy places; aṭana — for wandering; kautukena — with eagerness; dīna — of the wretched; eka — the only; bandhuḥ — friend; karuṇā — of compassion; eka — the one; sindhuḥ — ocean; tataḥ — from there; yayau — went; bhāgyavatīm — to the fortunate; avācīm — south; sva — of His own; nāma — name; ratna — of the jewel; grahaṇa — of the acceptance; utsava — for the festival; utkaḥ — eager.

1Thus, eager to wander to the holy places, He — the only friend of the wretched, the one ocean of compassion — went from there to the fortunate south, longing for the festival of [people's] accepting the jewel of His own name.

Verse 2

विलोक्य तं वर्त्मनि कृष्णसारा-
स्तृष्णावताक्ष्णोर्युगलेन भूयः ।
रूपामृतं पातुमिवाप्तधैर्याः
समं समन्तात् सविधं समीयुः ॥२॥

vilokya taṁ vartmani kṛṣṇa-sārās
tṛṣṇāvatākṣṇor yugalena bhūyaḥ |
rūpāmṛtaṁ pātum ivāpta-dhairyāḥ
samaṁ samantāt savidhaṁ samīyuḥ ||2||

vilokya — having seen; tam — Him; vartmani — on the road; kṛṣṇa-sārāḥ — the black antelopes; tṛṣṇāvatā — with the thirsting; akṣṇoḥ — of eyes; yugalena — with the pair; bhūyaḥ — again [and again]; rūpa — of [His] form; amṛtam — the nectar; pātum — to drink; iva — as if; āpta — having gained; dhairyāḥ — courage; samam — all together; samantāt — from all sides; savidham — close [to Him]; samīyuḥ — came.

2Seeing Him on the road, the black antelopes took courage, as if to drink again and again the nectar of His form with their thirsting pairs of eyes, and all together came close to Him from every side.

Verse 3

श्रीरङ्गक्षेत्रमसौ दयालुः
कावेरिकावेष्टितमुच्चदेशम् ।
आसाद्य तत्रत्यमवेक्ष्य देवं
प्रियाकरोऽसौ मुदमाप तुङ्गाम् ॥३॥

śrī-raṅga-kṣetram asau dayāluḥ
kāverikā-veṣṭitam ucca-deśam |
āsādya tatratyam avekṣya devaṁ
priyākaro 'sau mudam āpa tuṅgām ||3||

śrī-raṅga-kṣetram — Sri Ranga-kshetra; asau — He; dayāluḥ — the Merciful One; kāverikā — by the Kaveri; veṣṭitam — encircled; ucca — elevated; deśam — a place; āsādya — having reached; tatratyam — present there; avekṣya — having beheld; devam — the Deity; priya — of love (?); ākaraḥ — the mine; asau — He; mudam — joy; āpa — attained; tuṅgām — lofty.

3The Merciful One reached Sri Ranga-kshetra, an elevated place encircled by the Kaveri. Beholding the Deity there, He, the mine of love, attained lofty joy.

Note. Priyākara, literally "a mine of what is dear", that is, a treasury of love; or perhaps "one who does what is pleasing" (?). Shrirangam stands on an island between the arms of the Kaveri. The first pada has only ten syllables (śrī-raṅga-kṣetram asau dayāluḥ: ————⏑⏑—⏑——) instead of the eleven of the upajāti; a syllable seems to have dropped out (?).

Verse 4

त्रिमल्लभट्टस्य महाशयस्य
गृहे कृतावासविधिः कृपालुः ।
कुतूहलेनैव निनाय चातु-
र्मास्यं स आवश्यककर्म कुर्वन् ॥४॥

trimalla-bhaṭṭasya mahāśayasya
gṛhe kṛtāvāsa-vidhiḥ kṛpāluḥ |
kutūhalenaiva nināya cātur-
māsyaṁ sa āvaśyaka-karma kurvan ||4||

trimalla-bhaṭṭasya — of Trimalla Bhatta; mahāśayasya — the noble-minded; gṛhe — in the house; kṛta — having made; āvāsa — of residence; vidhiḥ — the arrangement (having settled); kṛpāluḥ — the Merciful One; kutūhalena — with eager delight; eva — indeed; nināya — spent; cāturmāsyam — the chaturmasya; saḥ — He; āvaśyaka — obligatory; karma — duties; kurvan — performing.

4Settling in the house of the noble-minded Trimalla Bhatta, the Merciful One spent the chaturmasya there with eager delight, performing the obligatory duties.

Note. In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 9.82–86) the host is Venkata Bhatta, but in the brief summary (Madhya 1.108–109) the Lord spends the chaturmasya with Trimalla Bhatta, as in Karnapura; according to Gaudiya tradition, Trimalla and Venkata were brothers (the third being Prabodhananda Sarasvati). The chaturmasya is the four months of the rainy season, during which sannyasis do not travel.

Verse 5

कावेरिकायां विहिताप्लवोऽयं
चकार तस्या बहुपावनत्वम् ।
श्रीरङ्गसङ्गं प्रविलोक्य देवं
निनाय मासांश्चतुरः कृपालुः ॥५॥

kāverikāyāṁ vihitāplavo 'yaṁ
cakāra tasyā bahu-pāvanatvam |
śrī-raṅga-saṅgaṁ [-saṁjñaṁ?] pravilokya devaṁ
nināya māsāṁś caturaḥ kṛpāluḥ ||5||

kāverikāyām — in the Kaveri; vihita — having performed; āplavaḥ — bathing; ayam — He; cakāra — made; tasyāḥ — its; bahu — manifold; pāvanatvam — purifying power; śrī-raṅga — Sri Ranga; saṅgam (saṁjñam?) — named (?); pravilokya — beholding; devam — the Deity; nināya — spent; māsān — months; caturaḥ — four; kṛpāluḥ — the Merciful One.

5Bathing in the Kaveri, He multiplied its purifying power. Beholding the Deity named Sri Ranga, the Merciful One spent four months [there].

Note. श्रीरङ्गसङ्गं in the edition is unintelligible. We conjecture śrī-raṅga-saṁjñam, "called Sri Ranga" (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 6

वर्षाशरन्मध्यगतः स कालः
परिष्वजन्तीं शरदं चुचुम्बे ।
कान्ताद्वयान्तःशयितो विलासी
पार्श्वाविवृत्ताविव वीतनिद्रः ॥६॥

varṣā-śaran-madhya-gataḥ sa kālaḥ
pariṣvajantīṁ śaradaṁ cucumbe |
kāntā-dvayāntaḥ-śayito vilāsī
pārśvāvivṛttāv iva vīta-nidraḥ ||6||

varṣā — of the rains; śarat — and of autumn; madhya — in the middle; gataḥ — situated; saḥ — that; kālaḥ — season; pariṣvajantīm — embracing [it]; śaradam — autumn; cucumbe — kissed; kāntā — of beloveds; dvaya — two; antaḥ — between; śayitaḥ — lying; vilāsī — a lover; pārśva — onto [his] side; āvivṛttau — on turning; iva — like; vīta — rid of; nidraḥ — sleep.

6That season lying between the rains and autumn kissed Autumn as she embraced him — like a lover lying between two beloveds who, waking and turning onto his side, [kisses the one who embraces him].

Note. That is, autumn set in. The edition has स काल without the visarga.

Verse 7

ततो नवोत्फुल्लसरोरुहास्या
नवोत्पलाक्षी गतपङ्कजाला ।
सुजीवना तत्करुणाप्तिकामा
दासीव भेजे शरदीश्वरं तत् ॥७॥

tato navotphulla-saroruhāsyā
navotpalākṣī gata-paṅka-jālā |
sujīvanā tat-karuṇāpti-kāmā
dāsīva bheje śarad īśvaraṁ tat ||7||

tataḥ — then; nava — freshly; utphulla — blossomed; saroruha — a lotus; āsyā — [whose] face [is]; nava — fresh; utpala — blue lotuses; akṣī — [whose] eyes [are]; gata — gone; paṅka — of mud (of sin); jālā — [whose] film [is]; su-jīvanā — [having] pure water (a good life); tat — His; karuṇā — mercy; āpti — to attain; kāmā — desiring; dāsī — a maidservant; iva — like; bheje — served; śarat — autumn; īśvaram — the Lord; tat — then (?).

7Then Autumn — her face a freshly blossomed lotus, her eyes fresh blue lotuses, the film of mud gone from her, her waters pure — served the Lord like a maidservant who desires to attain His mercy.

Note. A double meaning (śleṣa): paṅka is both "mud" and "sin", jīvana both "water" and "life". The maidservant is free of sin, lives righteously and serves her master for the sake of his favour. The final tat is unclear; one would expect tam (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 8

अथात आनन्दसमूहमग्नो
ययौ प्रहृष्टो दिशि दक्षिणस्याम् ।
महाप्रभुः स्वीयगुणानुगाथा-
निरन्तरोत्कीर्तनमुग्धवक्त्रः ॥८॥

athāta ānanda-samūha-magno
yayau prahṛṣṭo diśi dakṣiṇasyām |
mahāprabhuḥ svīya-guṇānugāthā-
nirantarotkīrtana-mugdha-vaktraḥ ||8||

atha ataḥ — then from here; ānanda — of bliss; samūha — in the mass; magnaḥ — immersed; yayau — went; prahṛṣṭaḥ — rejoicing; diśi dakṣiṇasyām — in the southern direction; mahāprabhuḥ — Mahaprabhu; svīya — of His own; guṇa — qualities; anugāthā — of songs; nirantara — by unceasing; utkīrtana — loud chanting; mugdha — charming; vaktraḥ — [whose] face [was].

8Then Mahaprabhu, immersed in a mass of bliss, went on from here, rejoicing, in the southern direction, His face charming with the unceasing loud chanting of songs about His own qualities.

Note. "His own qualities", that is, the qualities of Krishna.

Verse 9

तत्र क्वचित् श्रीरघुनाथभक्तं
प्रशान्तचित्तं द्विजपुङ्गवं सः ।
सीता दशास्यापहृतेति शोका-
द्बहिर्व्रजत्प्राणमिवालुलोके ॥९॥

tatra kvacit śrī-raghunātha-bhaktaṁ
praśānta-cittaṁ dvija-puṅgavaṁ saḥ |
sītā daśāsyāpahṛteti śokād
bahir-vrajat-prāṇam ivāluloke ||9||

tatra kvacit — somewhere there; śrī-raghunātha — of Sri Raghunatha; bhaktam — a devotee; praśānta — peaceful; cittam — [whose] mind [was]; dvija-puṅgavam — a best of brahmanas; saḥ — He; sītā — Sita; daśa-āsya — by the Ten-faced one; apahṛtā — has been abducted; iti — that; śokāt — from grief; bahiḥ — out; vrajat — going; prāṇam — [whose] life [was]; iva — as if; āluloke — saw.

9Somewhere there He saw a best of brahmanas, a devotee of Sri Raghunatha, peaceful in mind, whose life, from grief that Sita had been abducted by the Ten-faced one, seemed to be departing.

Note. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 9.179–215: in Southern Mathura a brahmana worshipper of Rama (Ramadasa) grieves over the abduction of Sita; later the Lord brings him the leaves of the Kurma Purana. The Ten-faced one is Ravana.

Verse 10

लक्ष्मीरियं राक्षसहस्तयाता
किमेतदित्यस्य मनो विदित्वा ।
आश्वासयन्नेव तमब्रवीद्भो
मैवं स्वरूपं शृणु यद्ब्रवीमि ॥१०॥

lakṣmīr iyaṁ rākṣasa-hasta-yātā
kim etad ity asya mano viditvā |
āśvāsayann eva tam abravīd bho
maivaṁ svarūpaṁ śṛṇu yad bravīmi ||10||

lakṣmīḥ — Lakshmi; iyam — she; rākṣasa — of a Rakshasa; hasta — into the hands; yātā — fallen; kim — what; etat — is this; iti — thus; asya — his; manaḥ — mind; viditvā — having understood; āśvāsayan — comforting; eva — indeed; tam — to him; abravīt — said; bho — O [brahmana]; mā evam — not so; svarūpam — the truth; śṛṇu — hear; yat — which; bravīmi — I tell.

10Understanding his mind — "She is Lakshmi, and she has fallen into the hands of a Rakshasa? What is this?" — He comforted him and said: "O [brahmana], not so! Hear the truth, which I shall tell you.

Verse 11

यद्वा मदीये वचसि प्रतीति-
र्न ते भवित्री तदिदं नु पश्य ।
पुराणपद्यद्वयमित्यकस्मा-
ददर्शयत् स्वाञ्चलतो विकृष्य ॥११॥

yadvā madīye vacasi pratītir
na te bhavitrī tad idaṁ nu paśya |
purāṇa-padya-dvayam ity akasmād
adarśayat svāñcalato vikṛṣya ||11||

yadvā — or if; madīye — in My; vacasi — word; pratītiḥ — faith; na — not; te — of you; bhavitrī — will be; tat — then; idam — this; nu — now; paśya — look at; purāṇa — from a Purana; padya — of verses; dvayam — a pair; iti — thus [saying]; akasmāt — suddenly; adarśayat — showed; sva — of His own; añcalataḥ — from the hem of the cloth; vikṛṣya — having drawn out.

11Or if you will not have faith in My word, then look at this now." So saying, He suddenly drew out from the hem of His cloth two verses from a Purana and showed [them to him].

Note. In the Chaitanya-charitamrita the order is different: the Lord hears the Kurma Purana in Rameshvaram, takes the old leaves with these verses and, returning to Southern Mathura, gives them to the brahmana Ramadasa (Madhya 9.200–215). In Karnapura the leaf is already with the Lord.

Verse 12

सीतयाराधितो वह्नि-
श्छायासीतामजीजनत् ।
तां जहार दशग्रीवः
सीता वह्निपुरं गता ॥१२॥

sītayārādhito vahniś
chāyā-sītām ajījanat |
tāṁ jahāra daśa-grīvaḥ
sītā vahni-puraṁ gatā ||12||

sītayā — by Sita; ārādhitaḥ — propitiated; vahniḥ — Agni; chāyā — a shadow; sītām — Sita; ajījanat — produced; tām — her; jahāra — carried off; daśa-grīvaḥ — the Ten-necked one; sītā — Sita; vahni — of Agni; puram — to the abode; gatā — went.

12"Agni, propitiated by Sita, produced a shadow Sita. Her the Ten-necked one carried off, while [the real] Sita went to the abode of Agni.

Note. Metre anuṣṭubh. This is a quotation: verses 12–13 are cited in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 9.211–212) as verses of the Kurma Purana (confirmed; the last pada of 13 there is different — see the note on 13).

Verse 13

परीक्षासमये वह्निं
छायासीता विवेश सा ।
वह्निः सीतां समानीय
स्वपुरादुदनीनमत् ॥१३॥

parīkṣā-samaye vahniṁ
chāyā-sītā viveśa sā |
vahniḥ sītāṁ samānīya
sva-purād udanīnamat ||13||

parīkṣā — of the ordeal; samaye — at the time; vahnim — into the fire; chāyā-sītā — the shadow Sita; viveśa — entered; sā — she; vahniḥ — Agni; sītām — Sita; samānīya — having brought; sva — from his own; purāt — abode; udanīnamat (read udanīnayat) — led out.

13At the time of the ordeal the shadow Sita entered the fire, and Agni, bringing [the real] Sita from his own abode, led her forth [to Rama]."

Note. The edition has उदनीनमत्; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads sva-purād udanīnayat, "led out from his abode" (the aorist of the causative of nī), and so we read. In the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 9.212) the last pada is different: tat-purastād anīnayat, "brought [her] before him", that is, before Rama.

Verse 14

अथात्र कथञ्चिद्यतिनां वरिष्ठं
ददर्श नाथो बहुहृष्टचित्तम् ।
महानुभावं परमं पुरस्ता-
दानन्दमध्यं च पुरीं तदन्तम् ॥१४॥

athātra kathañcid yatināṁ variṣṭhaṁ
dadarśa nātho bahu-hṛṣṭa-cittam |
mahānubhāvaṁ paramaṁ purastād
ānanda-madhyaṁ ca purīṁ tad-antam ||14||

atha — then; atra — here; kathañcit (read kañcit, as GGM) — a certain; yatinām — of ascetics; variṣṭham — the best; dadarśa — saw; nāthaḥ — the Master; bahu — very; hṛṣṭa — joyful; cittam — [whose] heart [was]; mahā-anubhāvam — magnanimous; paramam — "Parama"; purastāt — at the beginning; ānanda — "ananda"; madhyam — [having] in the middle; ca — and; purīm — "Puri"; tat-antam — [having] at its end.

14Then here the Master saw a certain best of ascetics, magnanimous and very joyful at heart, [whose name had] "Parama" at the beginning, "ananda" in the middle and "Puri" at its end.

Note. A riddle-name: Paramananda Puri, a disciple of Madhavendra Puri. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 9.168–174: the Lord meets Paramananda Puri at Rishabha hill; he goes on to Puri, and the Lord to the Setu. In our edition the first pada has twelve syllables (athātra kathañcid); the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads athātra kañcid, "a certain [best of ascetics]", which is metrically correct, and so we read.

Verse 15

विलोक्य संभाष्य सुजातहर्षौ
बभूवतुस्तौ परमप्रभावौ ।
अन्योन्यसंप्रीतिवशौ कृपालू
तस्मात् प्रयातुं दधतुश्च चेतः ॥१५॥

vilokya saṁbhāṣya sujāta-harṣau
